reconstructionBasis.moduleRule: A module is a product surface or a product capability that the owner can recognize and manage. A technical branch, Gate, Stage label, test run, or filename is never a project module by itself.
reconstructionBasis.promotionRule: When a task becomes a durable core capability with independent goals, risks, acceptance criteria, and multiple stages, it may be promoted to module level only after owner confirmation.
reconstructionBasis.technicalEvidencePolicy: Git branches, commits, Gate labels, Stage 1E, tests, and run records are implementation evidence attached to product work; they do not define the product hierarchy.
reconstructionBasis.ownerStatement: The intended product skeleton is a ten-page Guanxiang website. Pages 1-7 were completed; Page 8 was paused because the reading system did not meet the owner's expectations. On 2026-08-09 the owner formally promoted the reading system to Module 11 and made it the strategic product mainline, confirmed that Page 4 discernment Stage 1E must finish first and the reading module remains paused until then, and accepted the six reading-experience criteria as v0.1.

risks.statement: Technical experiment labels can replace the owner's product map, causing work to continue without a recognizable product outcome.
risks.mitigation: Use the ten-page product skeleton plus owner-confirmed promoted modules as the only project/module layer.

risks.statement: The project can keep optimizing Page 4 discernment while Page 8 remains blocked by the unvalidated reading system.
risks.mitigation: Owner confirmed the sequence: finish Page 4 Stage 1E first, keep Module 11 as the strategic mainline but paused, then resume the reading system.

risks.statement: The owner-confirmed v0.1 reading-system completion definition has not yet been validated by the required experiments and product acceptance.
risks.mitigation: Treat the six v0.1 criteria as the locked product target; every later experiment must trace to them, and any criteria change requires a new owner-confirmed version.

risks.statement: All August intelligence artifacts are untracked; raw run records include provider identifiers and must not be staged blindly.
risks.mitigation: Perform a separate provenance/privacy/asset review before any Git write action.

risks.statement: Current deployment, Release Gate, charging, persistence, and Gate 2 governance state are not reconciled.
risks.mitigation: Run a separate read-only release-state audit before claiming production completion.

risks.statement: Module-level PMO, manager, QA, asset manager, reviewers, and execution agents are unassigned.
risks.mitigation: Assign real responsibilities only after the module tree is owner-confirmed.

conflicts.statement: The previous reconstruction used technical stages as the project hierarchy, while the owner manages Guanxiang as ten product pages plus promotable core capabilities.
conflicts.resolution: Pages 1-10 remain product modules, and the owner formally promoted the reading system to Module 11.

conflicts.statement: Stage 1E was previously called the project mainline, but its scope is pre-divination discernment on Page 4 rather than Page 8 reading quality.
conflicts.resolution: Stage 1E remains under MOD-GX-P04 and executes first; MOD-GX-READING is the confirmed strategic mainline but stays paused until discernment completes.

conflicts.statement: Gate 2 stops at READY_FOR_BLIND_REVIEW and does not authorize formal product integration, while later main-ancestor commits launch personalized readings.
conflicts.resolution: A separate governance/release audit is required; later authorization must not be invented.

conflicts.statement: README and Phase 2C describe no live/public release and Narrative UNVERIFIED, while later source history contains live personalized-reading paths.
conflicts.resolution: Current external release state remains unconfirmed.

conflicts.statement: The latest Stage 0-1E records are untracked and therefore cannot be treated as committed project truth.
conflicts.resolution: Keep worktree and committed truth distinct until a separate asset/provenance review.

conflicts.statement: Page 9 and Page 10 names and responsibilities are inferred from hidden future sections rather than an owner-provided ten-page specification.
conflicts.resolution: Owner retained both proposed names provisionally and deferred detailed scope refinement.
